asset: KESTREL rigged character, F:/git/val etf/assets/characters/kestrel/ (kestrel.glb / kestrel.fbx / kestrel.blend, built by build_kestrel.py + kes_*.py). Review written to F:/git/val etf/assets/characters/kestrel/review/review.json, with the evidence sheet at review/renders/rv2_key_issues_sheet.png and the scripts rv2_weights.py, rv2_weights_b.py, rv2_render.py, rv2_socket.py, rv2_sheet.py, render_review.py and glb_inspect.py.

issues.issue: The chest plate is not rigid. Its edges carry clavicle/upperarm weights, so the plate crumples in a rifle-ready pose, which is the pose opponents see most. NOTES says the plate is rigid on spine_03, but only 205 verts were made rigid (build log 'chest 205').
issues.evidence: review/rv2_weights.py: plate right edge (37 verts): spine_03 mean 0.38, spine_02 0.36, upperarm_r 0.17 (max 0.24), clavicle_r max 0.25. Left edge: upperarm_l max 0.24, clavicle_l max 0.28. 171 verts at |x|<0.12 carry upperarm_r >= 0.2 (max 0.40). Renders: F:/git/val etf/assets/characters/kestrel/review/renders/pose_rifle_shoulder_r.png, pose_rifle_34.png.
issues.fix: In kes_skin.py, select the whole plate (bone-coloured texels in |x|<0.15, y<-0.07, 1.17<z<1.34 plus the connected inner layer). Weight it 100% spine_03, with at most 30% spine_02 on the bottom row. Strip clavicle/upperarm weights from all torso verts with |x|<0.13, then smooth only the jacket ring around the plate. Re-test with the right upper arm 30-45 deg forward.

issues.issue: Raising the arms (zipline hang, reaching up) tears the torso. A webbing forms from the armpit to the jet pack and the chest stretches. The elbow pads are split about 50/50 between upperarm and lowerarm.
issues.evidence: render_review.py metrics: zipline pose 1945 edges stretched >1.8x (max 428 mm), mostly spine_02/03 and upperarm_l/r. Rifle pose: 656 edges (max 195 mm). review/renders/heat_zipline_front34.png, pose_zipline_armpit_l.png, pose_zipline_shoulders_back.png. rv2_weights_b.py: upperarm/lowerarm weights 0.3-0.8 at (+-0.33..0.38, 0.175, 1.03..1.13).
issues.fix: Limit upperarm influence to verts within about 9 cm of the upper-arm segment, with a short falloff band at the armpit. Give the lat/back panel and the jet-pack strap area to spine_03/clavicle. Solve heat weights on a proxy with the arms raised about 45 deg, or add UE5 twist bones (upperarm_twist_01_l/r). Make the elbow pads rigid on lowerarm. Verify with arms overhead and a one-arm zipline hang.

issues.issue: The back of the bob stretches into vertical streaks and shears when the head pitches or yaws. TRELLIS fused the hair bottom into the collar, and that band is weighted to spine_03/neck while the hair above follows the head.
issues.evidence: review/renders/nape_down25.png, nape_down25_yaw35.png (nape_sheet.png). Stress pose (head 30 deg down): 808 head-dominant edges stretched >1.8x. weight_probe.py: lower back hair/collar band 786 verts at spine_03 mean 0.92 next to 256 head verts.
issues.fix: Split the hair shell from the collar along the navy-hair/charcoal-collar texture boundary, make the whole hair 100% head, and move the head-to-neck blend band below the hair, on the collar only. Check head pitch +-30 deg and yaw +-60 deg from behind.

issues.issue: The eyepiece breaks DIRECTION_LOG 3 ('small' lens, 'must not cover the brow or cheek'). The lens is about 35% larger than spec, reaches from the brow down to mid-nose height, and sits 2-3 cm proud of the face in a deep graphite housing that reads as a goggle cup, not a thin monocle frame. The straps float off the temple.
issues.evidence: Glass 6.7 x 5.0 cm, rim 7.4 x 5.4 cm (z 1.4855-1.5395), housing to y -0.0778; BRIEF frame is 5.6 x 4.0 cm. review/renders/rv2_lens_front_ortho_with.png vs rv2_lens_front_ortho_without.png, rv2_lens_side_ortho.png, rv2_cmp_head_vs_v06.png. tech_log.txt: housing/strap to skin distance median 2.9 mm, max 32 mm.
issues.fix: Shrink the lens to about 5.0 x 3.6 cm, centred on the painted eye (about (0.047, -0.056, 1.512)), 8-12 mm in front of the eye, with a 3 mm frame instead of the deep housing. To stop needing a big lens over the old TRELLIS disc, shrinkwrap the disc verts back onto a smoothed face surface (eye socket) and repaint the skin around it. Shrinkwrap the straps to skin + 1.5 mm.

issues.issue: The face does not read as v06's 'calm, determined' Kestrel. The lips protrude in a pout, the face is a soft round blob, a dark vertical streak runs down her right cheek like a scar or tear line, and her left temple (the tech side, seen in every 3/4 view) is a patchwork of jagged skin shards with a small open hole.
issues.evidence: review/renders/rv2_cmp_head_vs_v06.png, rv2_clay_face_front.png (the lip protrusion is in the geometry), cu_face_low.png, wire_head_her_left.png, orient_full_front.png (backface hole at the left temple), renders/kestrel_head_three_quarter.png.
issues.fix: Push the mouth verts back 3-4 mm and flatten the lip volume. Repaint a narrow straight mouth with slightly down-turned corners. Move the fringe strand off the cheek by 3 mm and fill the dark gap texels with skin. At the left temple, delete the creased shard faces between the lens and the ear, fill and smooth, then clone-fill skin from neighbouring texels.

issues.issue: Skin bleeds through the gloves as orange blotches across the palms, finger undersides and knuckles. That is far more than the 'few orange specks' in NOTES, and it shows on weapon-holding hands (first-person and close third-person).
issues.evidence: review/renders/cu_hand_l_palm.png, cu_hand_r_back.png, grip_L_in.png, grip_R_out.png, rv2_sprint_pouch_l.png; renders/pose_fists_l_v0.6_-1_0.3.png.
issues.fix: Extend the glove repaint in kes_fix.py to all palm-side and knuckle texels from the wrist band to the proximal finger joints, using a bone-distance mask rather than a colour mask. Push the inner skin layer 1 mm inward, or delete the inner skin faces under the glove shell, so it can't bleed through when posed.

issues.issue: Black glyph-like marks and grey grime remain on the outer and back faces of both jet-pack pods. From a third-person or chasing-enemy camera this is the most visible part of her, and the style guide says no photoreal grime.
issues.fix: Apply the pod clean-up mask to the full surface of both pod islands, not just the front band. Flat-fill with bone (0.55, 0.52, 0.46) plus soft AO, keep the dark side panels and the teal rings, and re-check from a back third-person camera.

issues.issue: The halo socket sits on the head bone 0.45 m from the head joint. Even 'position only', head pitch swings it far off the skull, so the halo will drift forward when she looks down.
issues.evidence: rv2_render.py halo set: head 30 deg down (neck 10 + head 20) puts the socket 11.0 cm forward of the skull top; 25 deg up puts it 9.3 cm back. render_review.py metrics: head-only pitch 15/30/45 deg moves the socket 11.7/23.3/34.4 cm. review/renders/rv2_halo_side_head_down30.png, rv2_halo_side_head_up25.png.
issues.fix: Choose one and document it in NOTES and the glTF extras: re-parent KES_SOCKET_Halo to neck_01/spine_03, or add KES_SOCKET_HaloAnchor at the skull top on head and define halo = anchor world position + 0.22 m world up.

issues.issue: The weapon sockets sit at the palm centre, about 2.2 cm below the web of the hand along the weapon's up axis. Per WEAPON_MODULAR_SPEC the weapon origin is the grip top where the web of the hand sits, so guns will sit low in the hand. Left and right also differ by 1.2 cm along the palm normal.
issues.evidence: review/rv2_socket.py: web point (thumb_01/index_01 midpoint) in socket-local (cm): R (2.9, -0.4, 2.2), L (1.7, -0.4, 2.3). review/renders/grip_sheet.png (mako_default.glb snapped to the sockets).
issues.fix: Move both sockets to the web point, inset about 1.5 cm along local +X into the grip volume, and make them mirror-symmetric. Verify with mako_default.glb in a curled-finger grip pose.

issues.issue: The left belt pouch is not rigid, contrary to NOTES: it is partly weighted to thigh_l and shears slightly when the knee lifts.
issues.evidence: rv2_weights_b.py: belt pouch L (567 verts) pelvis mean 0.64, thigh_l mean 0.27 (max 0.87). review/renders/rv2_sprint_pouch_l.png.
issues.fix: Grow the pouch mask to the whole pouch island and set it 100% pelvis, keeping the thigh blend on the trouser fabric only.

issues.issue: The lens rim and glass read pale mint/white, not the saturated teal of v06. Rim emission 3.5 (2.45 in the glb) clips to white, and the light paint behind the glass washes it out.
issues.fix: Set rim emission to about 1.2-1.8 in palette teal (0, 0.70, 0.62), glass alpha 0.35-0.4 on a slightly darker teal, and darken the painted sclera/disc behind the glass so the iris and pupil read.

issues.issue: 66,898 triangles against the 30-50k character target (under the 70k max), with no LODs. The body material is double-sided because of TRELLIS double layers.
issues.evidence: review/glb_inspect.py: KES_Body 66,000 + KES_Eyepiece 898 tris. M_KES_Body doubleSided: true.
issues.fix: Decimate the body to about 48k (face/hands protected, UVs kept) and add KES_Body_LOD1 (about 20k) and LOD2 (about 8k) on the same skin. Delete the inner duplicate shell faces where possible so the material can be single-sided.

issues.issue: The collar's teal piping is a wobbly, uneven painted stripe, with stray teal splotches on the collar fronts. v06 has a clean, constant-width rim and front-edge line.
issues.fix: Paint the piping as a constant 4 mm band from an object-space distance to the collar top edge, plus the front V edge, and remove isolated teal islands outside that band.

issues.issue: The FBX loses roughness/metallic/AO (the ORM map is not carried) and contains a duplicate KES_BaseColor image.
issues.evidence: review/tech_log.txt: FBX re-import images = KES_BaseColor, KES_BaseColor.001, KES_Emission, KES_Normal. The glb is fine.
issues.fix: For the FBX pass, wire Separate Color(ORM).G to Roughness and .B to Metallic, or export separate grayscale maps. Make sure only one base-colour image node exists.

issues.issue: Height is measured to the hair top (1.700), but the style guide says 1.70 m without hair volume and the BRIEF has the skull crown at 1.700 with the hair top at about 1.72, so she is about 2 cm short.
issues.evidence: review/tech_log.txt: body bbox max Z 1.7000 (hair top); halo socket 0.22 above the hair top.
issues.fix: Scale so the skull crown is about 1.70 (hair top about 1.72) and keep the halo socket at hair top + 0.22.

issues.issue: From the front the silhouette is generic: the asymmetric hair wedge barely reads, the left-forearm grapple knob from the brief is missing, and the jet pack only reads from the side and 3/4.
issues.fix: Optional, cheap: push the long right-side hair sweep about 2 cm lower and outward at the tips (it also shows off the teal tips), and add a small bone grapple housing on her left forearm (BRIEF 4j), rigid on lowerarm_l.

verdict: Not yet acceptable as a prototype character, but a solid base. What I confirmed works: I rebuilt it from the raw TRELLIS glb in a scratch copy and got byte-identical textures and a glb that matches to within 2.5e-8 m. The glTF is valid: a 53-joint skin, bind matrices that match the rest pose, normalised weights with at most 4 influences, and embedded textures. The UE5 bone names and the KES_SOCKET_Halo/WeaponR/WeaponL names and positions follow the specs. The outfit matches front_apose well. It can go into the engine now as a placeholder. Before a lead would sign off, it needs one fix pass: (1) a truly rigid chest plate (critical) and cleaner shoulder/armpit weights, because the rifle-ready pose crumples the plate and arms-up for ziplines tears the torso; (2) the hair split from the collar so the nape doesn't streak when she looks down; (3) a smaller lens that sits close to the face, as DIRECTION_LOG 3 asks, without covering brow or cheek, and a calmer, determined mouth; (4) a clean-up of the face/temple, glove and jet-pod paint. Re-anchoring the halo socket (it swings 11 cm off the skull at a 30° head pitch) and the weapon sockets (about 2 cm off the web of the hand) are quick wins.
